title: P99 smoothing: hybrid microbatch scheduler + kernel autotuner for embedding endpoint
creator: Ava Martinez
description: We are seeing persistent tail latency (P99) spikes on the /v1/embeddings endpoint for small-input requests under medium QPS. Baseline for embedding-v2 on A10 instances: P50=22ms, P95=85ms, P99=420ms. Goal: reduce P99 to <=250ms without increasing average latency or unit cost by more than 10%. Approach is a combined scheduler and kernel tuning initiative: implement a hybrid microbatch scheduler that uses per-request tail-sampling heuristics to group latency-critical small requests into opportunistic microbatches, and add an online kernel-parameter autotuner that selects kernel launch / workspace sizes based on recent sequence-length and KV-cache hit patterns.
acceptance_criteria: P99 for embedding-v2 on A10 fleet measured over 24h <= 250ms across three test regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast)
No regression in P50 or throughput (<=5% variance vs baseline)
Canary rollout plan documented and automated (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with fast rollback hooks
Quality regression detection: sample-based check that embedding cosine similarity distribution vs baseline has KL divergence < 0.01 for production prompt set
plan: Design hybrid scheduler sketch: tail-sampling policy + deadline-aware batch window (tail-window ms and batch-max-size)
Implement scheduler as a pluggable policy (scheduler.mode=hybrid_tail_sampling) behind feature flag
Add kernel autotuner service that observes sequence length histograms and KV-cache miss rate; tune block-size and workspace thresholds
E2E integration tests with unit and integration harnesses (simulated QPS using replay traffic)
Canary rollout with metrics dashboard and automated rollback if P99 increases by >10% over baseline
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed comparing deadline-first vs tail-sampling microbatching on replayed traffic. Tail-sampling had 18% improvement in observed P99 in the replay environment.
2026-02-20: Prototype scheduler committed (feature flag) and running in internal staging. Initial autotuner implemented with heuristic hill-climb; replaced with Bayesian optimizer planned.

2026-03-01: Integration tests added to CI; found edge case where very short requests (len<16) were delayed >200ms due to batch window. Added per-priority bypass and deadline clamp to avoid user-visible delay.
2026-03-08: Canary 1% started in us-east, telemetry collected for 24h. P99 reduced from 420ms to ~260ms on canary nodes; observed a minor increase in CPU for pre-processing + batch coalescing (~6%).

2026-03-12: Switched autotuner strategy from heuristic hill-climb to Gaussian Process Bayesian tuner to avoid oscillation; ran offline tuning job that suggested smaller workspace for seq<32 and larger launch config for seq>=512. Preparing 10% canary rollout.
technical_notes: Scheduler knobs: tail_window_ms (default 8ms), batch_max_size (default 64), priority_deadline_ms, sampling_rate for tail candidates
KV-cache impact: reducing microbatching window reduces merge opportunities but improves cache-locality; autotuner tracks KV-hit ratio and penalizes configs that increase cache misses
Implementation detail: scheduler runs on request ingress thread and hands off microbatches to worker pool; we added per-worker batch queues to reduce cross-thread merges, lowering contention.

Telemetry: added metric embeddings.scheduler.batch_size_histogram, embeddings.autotuner.selected_kernel, embeddings.kv_cache_hit_rate, and embeddings.latency.breakdown by component (ingest, batch, kernel, postprocess)
Fallback: if feature-flagged scheduler causes P99 regression during rollout, system will flip to legacy scheduler via fast-config and drain in-flight microbatches.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: microbatching can slightly change embedding numeric results due to (de)normalization or fused-kernel differences. Mitigation: run daily quality checks (cosine similarity sampling) and alert on KL divergence > 0.01.
Risk: autotuner may oscillate and destabilize latency. Mitigation: use conservative tuner learning rate, require min_samples before switching kernels, and add cooldown windows.
Risk: increased CPU for coalescing may affect cost. Mitigation: cap microbatching only to latency-critical traffic and expose config to Dedicated customers.
Risk: rollout dependent on region-specific load shapes. Mitigation: stagger canaries across regions and collect 24h of real traffic per step.
Operational: must add runbook for rollback and safe draining; owner is oncall-infra + assignee.
experiments: Experiment A: baseline vs hybrid_tail_sampling on replayed peak hour traffic. Metric: P99, P95, average CPU, KV-hit. Result: P99 -18% in staging replay.

Experiment B: autotuner off vs autotuner-bayesian online on canary nodes. Metric: sustained P99, kernel-switch frequency, throughput. Result: suggested kernel profiles reduced kernel time for long seq by ~12%.

Experiment C: deadline-aware bypass for high-priority small reqs to ensure no added user-visible latency. Metric: rate of bypassed requests and their P99. Result: bypass stabilized P99 for len<16 without losing coalescing benefits for other requests.
monitoring_and_dashboards: Perf dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/embeddings/p99_smoothing (contains region filters, fleet vs canary breakdown)
Canary alert: embeddings.p99.change > 10% sustained for 15m triggers rollback playbook
Quality dashboard: https://perfdash.internal.redwood/embeddings/quality-similarity (daily bucketed KL divergence, sample delta)
